issues.t: Automatic slipping or missing gears (TSB 02-13-8)
issues.sym: Slipping, a missing second or third gear, delayed shifts and a check-engine light with gear-ratio codes.
issues.why: Low internal line pressure in the automatic transmission can keep clutches and bands from holding. Ford issued a service bulletin covering these years.
issues.next: Have the transmission diagnosed and ask the shop about TSB 02-13-8. Catching it early may avoid a full rebuild.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak at the cooler line fitting (TSB 01-10-2)
issues.sym: Red fluid drips near the transmission or radiator lines and a low transmission fluid level.
issues.why: On some early-build trucks the cooler line connection at the transmission case can leak. Ford issued a service bulletin for it.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the fitting repaired soon. Running the transmission low on fluid can damage it.

issues.t: 5R55W/5R55S five-speed slipping, no third gear or harsh reverse
issues.sym: Engine flare on the 2-3 shift, slipping, no third gear, delayed or harsh reverse, or the transmission failing outright.
issues.why: These five-speed automatics are known for worn servo bores, broken intermediate bands and valve body leaks. Transmission failure is the most reported problem for this generation.
issues.next: Have shifting problems checked early by a shop that knows this transmission and ask about Ford TSBs 03-25-4 and 05-21-8. Some fixes cost far less than a rebuild if caught early.

issues.t: Liftgate glass hinges and panel crack (recall 04S20)
issues.sym: Cracks in the liftgate panel below the rear window, broken glass hinges, the rear glass shattering when opened or closed, or water getting in.
issues.why: The liftgate glass hinges and the panel around them can crack from stress. Ford recalled the hinge and ball stud bracket, but complaints continued after the repair.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 04S20. Avoid opening the rear glass if the hinges are cracked and have the liftgate inspected.

issues.t: Harsh or lunging shifts (TSB 07-6-3)
issues.sym: Hard jolts when shifting, the vehicle lunging forward, and transmission trouble codes.
issues.why: Harsh shifting is the top owner complaint for 2006. Ford issued a bulletin for valve body contamination in the six-speed automatic used with the V8.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned and ask about TSB 07-6-3. Have harsh engagements checked before they wear the transmission further.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park (TSB 06-25-10)
issues.sym: The shift lever will not move out of Park, so the manual release has to be used.
issues.why: Ford issued a service bulletin for shifters that stick in Park on these years.
issues.next: Use the manual shift-lock release if needed and ask a dealer about TSB 06-25-10.

issues.t: Sluggish take-off and harsh bump at low speed (TSB 11-12-10)
issues.sym: A slow start from a stop, then a harsh bump or slip, mostly after a rolling stop.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic shift calibration can cause poor low-speed engagement. Ford released a bulletin with a fix.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer about TSB 11-12-10 and a software update.

issues.t: "Shift to Park" message and dead battery (TSBs 15-0047, 17-2219)
issues.sym: A "Shift to Park" message even when in Park, the vehicle will not fully shut off, and the battery runs down overnight.
issues.why: The switch that tells the vehicle the shifter is in Park can fail or misread, so the vehicle thinks it is still in gear.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about TSBs 15-0047 and 17-2219. Have it fixed soon to avoid repeated dead batteries.

issues.t: Long cranking and harsh cold downshifts (TSB 13-5-31)
issues.sym: The engine cranks longer than normal before starting, and downshifts feel harsh or late when cold.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for these symptoms on the turbocharged 3.5L.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer about TSB 13-5-31.

issues.t: Engine block heater can leak coolant and short (recalls 25V-685, 26V-012)
issues.sym: Coolant leaking near the block heater, a low coolant level, or a tripped outlet when the heater cord is plugged in.
issues.why: The engine block heater can leak coolant into its electrical connection and short out.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls. Do not plug in the block heater until the repair is done.

issues.t: Seat recliner may not lock (recall 19V-633)
issues.sym: A seat back that does not lock firmly or moves unexpectedly.
issues.why: A part in the seat recliner may be missing, so the seat back may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Rear axle bolt can break (recalls 22V-255, 23V-199, 23V-675)
issues.sym: A loud clunk or heavy vibration from the rear when accelerating, sudden loss of drive, or the vehicle rolling while in Park.
issues.why: A rear axle mounting bolt can fracture, letting the axle housing shift and the driveshaft or axle shafts disconnect. The main fix is software that sets the parking brake each time you shift to Park, and Ford extended coverage on the bolt for some vehicles.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park, check the VIN for all of these recalls, and stop driving if a new rear clunk appears.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft may fracture (recall 20V-693)
issues.sym: Vibration or clunking from under the vehicle, then loss of drive or the vehicle rolling in Park.
issues.why: A driveshaft on some all-wheel-drive models may fracture.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and use the parking brake until it is fixed.

issues.t: Park pawl may engage while moving (recall 26V-402)
issues.sym: A sudden jolt or loss of drive while driving.
issues.why: The transmission park mechanism may engage while the vehicle is moving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the repair right away.

issues.t: Engine computer reset can cut power (recall 23V-069)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive power while driving, sometimes with warning messages.
issues.why: The powertrain control module can reset while driving on vehicles with the 2.3L and ten-speed automatic.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the software update. Pull over safely if power cuts out.

issues.t: Rearview or 360-degree camera image fails (several recalls)
issues.sym: A blank, frozen, flipped or blue backup camera image.
issues.why: Loose connections, wiring errors and software faults have led to many camera recalls on this generation.
issues.next: Check the VIN for camera recalls such as 23V-342, 25V-442, 26V-123 and 24V-801. Back up using mirrors with extra care until fixed.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can fail (recall 26V-117)
issues.sym: Wipers that stop working, often in rain or snow.
issues.why: The front wiper motor may fail.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the repair before driving in bad weather.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt anchor bolts (recalls 25V-093, 26V-159)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; a seat belt anchor may feel loose.
issues.why: Second-row seat belt anchor or buckle bolts may not be installed or tightened correctly, so the belt may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and get them done promptly.

issues.t: Intake valve can break (recall 24V-635)
issues.sym: A rough-running engine, misfire light, knocking, or sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Intake valves on some turbocharged V6 engines may fracture and damage the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Stop driving and have it towed if the engine suddenly runs rough or knocks.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail (recall 25V-455)
issues.sym: Stalling, hesitation or a no-start.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump may fail and stop fuel delivery.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Have it towed if it stalls and will not restart.

issues.t: Fuel line or filler tube may come loose (recalls 22V-685, 22V-088)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell or fuel dripping under the vehicle.
issues.why: A loose fuel line on the 2.3L or a filler tube that can detach may leak fuel, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel and check the VIN for these recalls.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply line may leak (recall 23V-597)
issues.sym: Oil on the engine or a burning oil smell or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The oil supply line to the turbocharger may leak oil onto hot parts.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Pull over and shut off the engine if you see smoke.

issues.t: Transmission valve body machining error (recall 25V-164)
issues.sym: Unusual shifting or drive problems.
issues.why: A transmission valve body may have been machined incorrectly at the factory.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it repaired soon.

issues.t: Powertrain computer reset while driving (recalls 26V-371, 25V-239)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: The powertrain control module can reset while the vehicle is moving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and get the software update. Pull over safely if power cuts out.

issues.t: Trailer hitch bolts may be loose (recall 25V-687)
issues.sym: Clunking from the hitch area when towing.
issues.why: Bolts holding the trailer hitch may not be tightened correctly, so the hitch could come loose under load.
issues.next: Do not tow until the VIN has been checked for this recall and the hitch is inspected.

issues.t: Engine failure from bearing or connecting rod defects (recalls 25V-344, 26V-343)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure warning, or sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Some engines were built with defective connecting rods or bearings that can fail.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls. Stop driving at once if you hear knocking or see an oil pressure warning.

issues.t: Front brake caliper and chassis bolts (recalls 25V-371, 25V-316, 25V-020)
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from the front, a pull while braking, or vibration.
issues.why: Front brake caliper bolts, a front subframe bolt or transmission crossmember bolts may not be tightened properly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and have the work done before driving much.

issues.t: Adaptive headlights may turn the wrong way (recall 26V-121)
issues.sym: Headlights swing away from the direction of a curve.
issues.why: A software fault can turn the adaptive headlights the wrong way in curves.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get the update.

issues.t: Driver seat may recline on its own (recall 26V-470)
issues.sym: The driver seat back moves rearward unexpectedly.
issues.why: A fault in the driver seat recliner can let the seat back recline without the driver using the control.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get it fixed before regular driving.
